text:
Predicates:
MountainRange(x) ::: x is a mountain range.
Location(x, y) ::: x is located in y.
Visited(x, y) ::: x visited y.
Mine(x) ::: x is a mine.
Donated(x) ::: x has been donated.
Premises:
(MountainRange(picuris) ∧ (Location(picuris, newMexico) ∨ Location(picuris, texas))) ::: The Picuris Mountains are a mountain range in New Mexico or Texas.
Visited(juandeonate, picuris) ::: Juan de Onate visited the Picuris Mountains.
(Mine(hardingPegmatiteMine) ∧ Location(hardingPegmatiteMine, picuris) ∧ Donated(hardingPegmatiteMine)) ::: The Harding Pegmatite Mine, located in the Picuris Mountains, was donated.
∀x (MountainRange(x) ∧ Location(x, texas) → ¬∃y (Mine(y) ∧ Location(y, x) ∧ Donated(y))) ::: There are no mountain ranges in texas that have mines which have been donated.
Conclusion:
∃x (MountainRange(x) ∧ Location(x, newMexico) ∧ Visited(juandeonate, x)) ::: Juan de Onate visited a mountain range in New Mexico.
